prompt: The planner launches the upload in `viewModelScope` and the student swipes the app away. What happens to the upload?
hint: Where does a coroutine live?

choices.text: It ends with the process, half done
choices.why: Right: a coroutine lives in the process, and the process is the system's to end.

choices.text: It moves to a system thread and finishes there
choices.why: No coroutine leaves its process; the system has no thread that adopts it.

choices.text: It is paused, and resumes the next time the app opens
choices.why: Nothing was saved, so there is nothing to resume.

choices.text: It keeps running, because it is on a background thread
choices.why: A background thread is still a thread of the process that just ended.

prompt: Why does a WorkManager request survive the phone rebooting?
hint: Where is the request kept, and who is told when the phone starts?

choices.text: Google Play services keep a copy and restore it
choices.why: WorkManager does not depend on Play services; the copy is its own.

choices.text: WorkManager's database and a boot receiver
choices.why: Right: the request is on disk, and `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED` is how WorkManager hears the phone started.

choices.text: The system's job scheduler keeps jobs across reboots by itself
choices.why: WorkManager does not rely on that; it reschedules from its own database.

choices.text: The request lives in `SharedPreferences`
choices.why: WorkManager keeps requests in a SQLite database of its own.

prompt: Match each job to the tool section 02 gives it.
hint: Ask: is somebody waiting to see it, must it be exact, must it run eventually?

pairs.left: Load the course list the student is looking at
pairs.right: A coroutine in the screen's scope

pairs.left: Send new sessions some time when there is a network

right_distractors: A periodic request every five minutes

prompt: `doWork` catches an `IOException` on attempt 1 of 3. What does `SyncWorker` return?
hint: Attempts are counted from 0.

choices.text: `Result.failure()`
choices.why: That is attempt 2, the last of three.

choices.text: `Result.retry()`
choices.why: Right: `1 < 3 - 1`, so it asks to be tried again.

choices.text: `Result.success()` with `sent : 0`
choices.why: Nothing was sent; reporting success would hide the failure.

choices.text: It throws the exception on to WorkManager
choices.why: The `catch` keeps it in the worker; an exception that escapes counts as failure.

prompt: Why does `SyncWorker` retry only on `IOException`, and let any other exception fail it?
hint: Which failures can a later attempt fix?

choices.text: WorkManager forbids retrying any other exception type
choices.why: The worker decides; WorkManager retries whatever answers `retry`.

choices.text: A network problem passes; a bug repeats itself
choices.why: Right: retrying an `IllegalStateException` only spends the battery.

choices.text: Other exceptions crash the app, so retrying them is impossible
choices.why: An exception escaping `doWork` is recorded as a failure; the app does not crash.

choices.text: `IOException` is the only checked exception in Kotlin
choices.why: Kotlin has no checked exceptions at all; `@Throws` is for Java callers.

prompt: `PlannerWorkerFactory.createWorker` returns `null` for `SummaryWorker`. What does WorkManager do?
hint: Section 03 says `null` is not an error.

choices.text: Fails the request with `FAILED`
choices.why: The chain test shows `SummaryWorker` succeeding.

choices.text: By reflection, as usual
choices.why: Right: that is how a worker with no extra dependency is still created.

choices.text: Asks Hilt for it
choices.why: This project has no Hilt; the fallback is WorkManager's own default factory.

choices.text: Retries `createWorker` until it returns a worker
choices.why: It asks once, then falls back.

prompt: In `SyncWorkerTest`, how many sessions did the output of the successful attempt say were sent?
hint: `Data {sent : …}`

prompt: Who checks that `NetworkType.CONNECTED` holds before `SyncWorker` runs?
hint: Not your code.

choices.text: `doWork`, in its first line
choices.why: The worker never sees the constraint; it is not called until it holds.

choices.text: The system, through WorkManager
choices.why: Right: constraints are checked by the system, not by your code.

choices.text: The `Uploader`, which fails without a network
choices.why: It would fail, but that is the retry path, not the constraint.

choices.text: `PlannerApp.onCreate`
choices.why: `onCreate` only schedules the request.

prompt: A periodic sync has run once. Six hours pass while the phone has no network. What does the test of section 04 say happens?
hint: Look at the line after `six hours later`.

choices.text: It runs anyway, because the period is over
choices.why: Uploads stayed at 1 until the constraints were met again.

choices.text: The request is `SUCCEEDED` and is removed
choices.why: A periodic request never reaches `SUCCEEDED`; it went back to `ENQUEUED`.

choices.text: It waits, `ENQUEUED`, until the network is back
choices.why: Right: each period waits for its constraints again.

choices.text: The period is skipped and the next one starts in six hours
choices.why: Nothing was skipped: the second upload ran as soon as the constraints were met.

prompt: `scheduleSync` is called from `onCreate`, which runs on every process start. What stops the planner from piling up periodic requests?
hint: The request has a name.

choices.text: Unique work with `KEEP`, which leaves the first one alone
choices.why: Right: three calls left one request, with the first id.

choices.text: WorkManager merges identical requests by comparing their workers
choices.why: Without a unique name, every `enqueue` adds a new request.

choices.text: `onCreate` runs once per installation
choices.why: It runs every time the process starts.

choices.text: The constraints reject a duplicate
choices.why: Constraints are about the phone's state, not about other requests.

prompt: A periodic request asks for 5 minutes. How many minutes does WorkManager actually use?
hint: The third test printed it.

prompt: With `BackoffPolicy.___` and 30 seconds, a retry waits 30 seconds, then 60, then 120.
hint: The other policy adds 30 each time.

prompt: In the chain, how does `SummaryWorker` know how many sessions were sent?
hint: `inputData`

choices.text: It calls the `Uploader` again
choices.why: That would send twice; it only reads.

choices.text: Its input is the sync's output `Data`
choices.why: Right: in a chain, each request's output is the next one's input.

choices.text: Both workers share a `companion object` variable
choices.why: Only the key's name is shared; values cannot survive a process restart that way.

choices.text: It reads the count from WorkManager's log
choices.why: Workers communicate through `Data`, not logs.

prompt: The server is down. Right after the chain is enqueued, what are the states of the sync and the summary?
hint: A retry is not a failure.

choices.text: `FAILED` and `FAILED`
choices.why: That is what a `failure` would do; the sync asked for a retry.

choices.text: `ENQUEUED` and `BLOCKED`
choices.why: Right: the sync waits for its back-off, and the summary waits for the sync.

choices.text: `RUNNING` and `ENQUEUED`
choices.why: With a synchronous executor nothing is still running when the test reads it.

choices.text: `ENQUEUED` and `SUCCEEDED` with an empty message
choices.why: The summary never ran; it is held behind the sync.

prompt: A student taps "sync now" twice in a second. The chain uses `beginUniqueWork("sync-now", REPLACE, …)`. What happens?
hint: `REPLACE` cancels what is still waiting.

choices.text: Two chains run, and the sessions are sent twice
choices.why: A unique name allows one chain at a time.

choices.text: The second tap is ignored
choices.why: That is `KEEP`; `REPLACE` does the opposite.

choices.text: The unfinished first chain is cancelled; a fresh one runs
choices.why: Right: the old one ends `CANCELLED`, and one send happens.

choices.text: WorkManager refuses the second chain and throws an exception at the button
choices.why: Unique work is a policy, not an error.

prompt: Order the life of a one-time request whose first attempt hits a dead network and whose second succeeds.
hint: It is `ENQUEUED` more than once.

prompt: You give `PlannerApp` a `Configuration.Provider` but leave the manifest without the `tools:node="remove"` entry. What goes wrong?
hint: Something initialises WorkManager before your `Application` has a say.

choices.text: The build fails because two configurations exist
choices.why: Nothing fails at build time; the problem appears when a worker is built.

choices.text: Nothing: `Configuration.Provider` always wins
choices.why: The library's initialiser sets WorkManager up first, with the default configuration.

choices.text: Your factory is never used, so `SyncWorker` cannot be built
choices.why: Right: the default factory only knows the two-parameter constructor.

choices.text: The app asks the student for a startup permission
choices.why: There is no such permission; this is a manifest-merging question.

prompt: Which permissions did adding WorkManager put into the merged manifest? Choose all that apply.
hint: Section 06 listed the merged manifest's permissions.

choices.text: `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED`
choices.why: Yes: it is how WorkManager reschedules after a reboot.

choices.text: `INTERNET`
choices.why: No: WorkManager checks the network, it does not use it; lesson 13 adds this one.

choices.text: `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE`
choices.why: Yes: it lets WorkManager check the network constraint.

choices.text: `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`
choices.why: No: that is lesson 19's, and the app has to ask for it.

prompt: `grep -c WorkManagerInitializer` on the merged manifest printed what number?
hint: The library's own manifest printed 1.

prompt: Which of these stops the planner's sync from ever running until the student opens the app again?
hint: One row of the table is in bold.

choices.text: The phone rebooting overnight
choices.why: The boot receiver reschedules everything.

choices.text: The system ending the process for memory
choices.why: The request is on disk; the system restarts the work.

choices.text: Force stop in the app's settings
choices.why: Right: every job is cancelled, and Android honours it completely.

choices.text: Doze, while the phone lies still
choices.why: Doze delays work to maintenance windows; it does not cancel it.

prompt: A tester reports that the sync runs on one phone and stops on another brand, with the same app. What is the likeliest cause section 07 names?
hint: Something does to apps what Force stop does.

choices.text: The maker's battery manager
choices.why: Right: it has the effect of Force stop, and nothing in code overrides it.

choices.text: The second phone's Android lacks WorkManager
choices.why: WorkManager ships inside the app, not with Android.

choices.text: The period of six hours is too long for that brand
choices.why: A period is not brand-specific; fifteen minutes is the only floor.

choices.text: `KEEP` behaves differently across makers
choices.why: Unique-work policies are WorkManager's code, the same everywhere.

prompt: A colleague writes a worker that sends "the session added at 09:14" by its id. Section 07 suggests something else. Why?
hint: Workers run late, and sometimes more than once.

choices.text: Workers cannot receive ids in `Data`
choices.why: A short id fits in `Data` easily.

choices.text: Sending whatever is unsent stays correct when it runs late or twice
choices.why: Right: by the time it runs, the session may have changed or been sent already.

choices.text: One worker per session would exceed the 15-minute floor
choices.why: The floor is about periodic requests, not how many one-time ones exist.

choices.text: The id would be lost if the process died
choices.why: Input `Data` is stored in WorkManager's database and survives.

prompt: Match each `Result` to what WorkManager does next.
hint: One of them is final.

pairs.right: Stores the output and starts the next request in the chain
Puts the request back to run after the back-off delay
Never runs it again, and fails what is chained after it

right_distractors: Asks the student whether to try again
